exactGap: Governed app build/publish exists only as plan item S5.4 (a separate post-foundation slice); the only code near it is gateway studio.rs, an explicitly ephemeral canvas with no hosting, versioning or visibility, and the blueprint Draft/Published/Rollback card is static copy. Agent definitions are mutable in place in Application Plane Convex (agents.update; status active/inactive/draft is a flag, not a revision), spaceAgentBindings.agentId carries no revision pin, and the gateway reads the live systemPrompt via agentPersonaForGateway on every invocation, so no draft/published split exists. The item is therefore not a stub of an existing pipeline: apps are docs-only and agent-definition revisions are absent.
reuse: Application Plane Convex agents + spaceAgentBindings + agentPersonaForGateway as the single place to add revisions and pin them
Data Plane wiki_page_versions / wiki_proposals draft-review-publish model as the precedent for propose, approve, publish and rollback
operating-map-client currentVersion pointer plus proposals as a UI precedent for a pointer-flip publish
ADR-0002 Application-owned cross-Space agent registry for installation counts and "which Spaces pin which revision"
sandbox-manager PromoteWorkspace RPC for promoting a built artifact out of the Space workspace (S5.4 build side)
Space binding status enum (pending, active, paused, revoked, failed) already rendered in AgentInstallationsPage
constraints: Application Plane owns agent definitions and the cross-Space registry (ADR-0002), so revisions cannot live in a Model Plane agent registry; Model only receives persona and profile per invoke. The binding schema states a stored-but-unenforced policy is a false promise, so a revision pin must ship together with its enforcement in agentPersonaForGateway. Publishing to an org or Space is a human-authorized Control decision, never agent-initiated, and a published app must not make private resources transitive (Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL). App hosting needs an isolated origin, egress policy and ZDR handling from Infra, which does not exist; Studio Plane and studio-core are proposal-only and Studio Plane forbids becoming a distributed monolith.
approachAdjustment: Split the item. (1) Shared agent definition draft/published revisions: put them in Application Plane Convex (revision rows or draft fields on agents, a publishedRevision pointer, a revision pin on spaceAgentBindings, resolution inside agentPersonaForGateway), NOT in a Model Plane agent registry, which does not exist; add a Control decision only when org-wide visibility is introduced. (2) Agent-built internal apps stay as S5.4 and should be treated as post-foundation, gated on room artifacts, sandbox promotion and an isolated hosting origin.
effortNote: XL stands for the apps half. The agent-definition revisions half is separable and roughly M (Convex tables plus gateway resolution plus a Publish changes UI), so it should be its own row.
verdictReason: Placement of the agent-definition half is wrong (Application Plane, not Model Plane) and the item bundles a docs-only XL apps lifecycle with a separable M revision feature; the current status "stub" overstates what exists.

exactGap: org-core has single-level orgs with only active versus soft-deleted state (organizations.status default, deleted_at, RestoreOrganization) and no archive or owner-transfer, which the gateway and settings UI explicitly defer. A parent-like construct already exists in Control: auth-core org_group (host-org anchored) with per-org data_access and billing_consolidation grants, mirrored into billing-core billing_group_memberships and consumed by the account.data.read decision, but with no product UI. There are no cross-org Spaces or guests (registered Spaces are org-bound and presence treats cross-org rows as impossible), and external chat connections exist only as integration-corev2 data/inbox providers (Slack, Teams message read, Meta/WhatsApp), not as Space bridges.
reuse: auth-core org_group and org_group_grant (host-org account above orgs) instead of a new parent-org table
billing-core billing_group_memberships (plan inheritance mirror) and the account.data.read decision path
org-core deletion_ledger lifecycle (soft delete, restore, reminders) as the template for an archived and transfer_pending state machine
integration-corev2 Slack, Teams and Meta connections plus webhookorg resolver as the ingest side of external chat
user-core decision.go SignDecision for a decision that carries both orgs policy
constraints: Control is the only external-link authority and Application owns conversation mapping and delivery receipts per the adopted S5.1 surface-neutral ingress ADR (known only through the adoption plan; the ADR file lives outside the repo and was not read). Space membership is org-bound in Control, so cross-org rooms need a new Control membership and decision model (one org ZDR must hold for content its members post) and cannot be bolted onto Application projections. Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL, and an external audience must restrict agents to a context without org memory or keys. Channel Plane is docs-only and its vision covers customer-facing widget and commerce channels, not Slack or Teams workspace bridges.
approachAdjustment: Replace "defer a parent-org table" with "reuse the shipped org_group and add UI plus lifecycle". Drop the blanket claim that external chat workspace connections must wait for Channel Plane: Channel Plane vision targets widgets, Shopify, WooCommerce and WordPress, and S5.1 left open whether the adapter lives in Channel Plane or elsewhere while assigning identity links to Control and mapping/delivery to Application. The cheap slice (org archive plus owner transfer) is independent of guests and should be its own row.
effortNote: XL stands only for shared cross-org rooms. Org archive plus owner transfer is M (org-core state, auth-core owner-role swap, gateway contract, settings UI); an org_group admin UI is S to M.
verdictReason: Status partial is right, but the item misses the existing org_group parent construct and mislabels where external chat connections belong; it should be reworded and split into org lifecycle (M), org_group UI (S to M) and shared rooms (XL, post-guests).

exactGap: Per facet: audit-core keeps only a per-event sha256 payload_hash used for idempotent conflict detection (no prev_hash, entry_hash, checkpoint or verify route; only GET and POST /v1/audit), and no TLA+, Alloy or Tamarin artefacts exist under apps. Supply-chain gates are partial and uneven: blocking pnpm audit (high) and gitleaks for the frontend and repo, weekly Dependabot only for frontend npm, gateway cargo and actions, Quarry-only cargo audit plus a continue-on-error govulncheck, pnpm 11 with a minimumReleaseAgeExclude list (INF: a release-age gate is active though no value is set), and no cargo-deny, image signing or gates for Control, Model or Data services. Residency is a label (org-core data_residency column unused, Space EffectPolicy residency string bound into decisions, deploy-wide EU region allowlist and one AZURE region per process in inference-core, no per-org routing), and integration-corev2 already tracks connection status needs_refresh plus access_token_expires_at with reconnect warnings in Settings and Inbox, so only proactive expiry warnings and Space credential grants (S3.4, plan only) are missing.
reuse: audit-core payload_hash, source_stream_sequence and ON CONFLICT dedupe as the starting point for an entry hash
user-core decision.go Ed25519 SigningKey and VerifyDecision for signing daily audit head checkpoints
inference-core EU_AZURE_REGIONS, deny-by-default non-EU embedding gate and Space EffectPolicy.Residency as the residency foundation
org-core data_residency column (dormant) as the per-org pin source
integration-corev2 Connection status plus AccessTokenExpiresAt and the existing isFailedIntegrationStatus UI for credential expiry states
existing CI workflows verevonv3-security.yml, secret-scan.yml, quarry-v2-ci.yml and dependabot.yml as the ones to extend
constraints: audit-core is Control-owned and ingests at-least-once from NATS with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so a hash chain needs per-org serialised append in insert order and will limit throughput; audit events must stay ids and hashes only (audit is not a shadow store, retention-schedule). Residency pinning is a Control policy that Model Plane enforces at routing time; Model must not read org-core tables, so the pin has to arrive through claims or a Control decision. Credential expiry belongs with the Control-owned credential grants planned in S3.4 (reuse resource grants, no new keychain). Sub-processor residency (Novu, Convex) limits any EU-only claim.
approachAdjustment: Treat as five independent rows rather than one L item: (1) audit hash chain, (2) formal decision model, (3) supply-chain gates, (4) per-org residency, (5) credential expiry. Start supply chain by tightening what exists (make Quarry govulncheck blocking, add cargo audit and govulncheck to Model, Control and Data CI, add an explicit minimumReleaseAge value and Dependabot cooldown) before adding cargo-deny and image signing. Fold credential expiry into S3.4 and state that reactive needs_refresh already ships. Make residency start from the org-core column and Space EffectPolicy residency and move inference-core from one region per process to a per-org selection.
effortNote: L holds only as an aggregate. Individually: hash chain M, formal spec M, supply-chain gates M, residency L (multi-region deployments are out of scope; routing only is M), credential warnings S.
verdictReason: Status partial is right, but three facets are further along than the item implies (supply-chain checks, residency label and gates, credential status) and the bundle hides five unrelated owners; split it and correct the facet statuses.

exactGap: Control user-core already has Space-keyed legal holds (space_legal_holds table, PUT and DELETE /spaces/:space_ref/legal-hold, operator audit events) but they only block the personal-Space deletion saga, and no message retention sweeper exists for a hold to pin (the retention schedule marks conversation and audit sweeps as TBC). There is no compliance principal or decision class, room export or search, custodian hold, information barrier, nor any admin hibernate, kill or transcript-read RPC (sandboxes.proto has lease, snapshot, workspace and process RPCs only, and ReleaseLease is org and owner scoped). The only export RPCs are the per-user privacy export and an in-memory RL trajectory export, neither of which is a compliance export.
reuse: user-core decision.go SignDecision and VerifyDecision plus the shared_thread_read_decision.go pattern (own action id, schema hash and permission so a member read token can never be replayed as a compliance read)
space_legal_holds and space_deletion_operator_events as the base to generalise into custodian or scoped holds
Application Plane spaceDeletionReceipts per-owner receipt aggregation for export or hold propagation across planes
session-core thread read path (verify_thread_read_space_decision and threads.space_id scoping) as the owner-plane export site
audit-core GET /v1/audit with delegation verification for access logging
Data Plane quickwit-adapter-rs admin authorization (admin scope, mandatory admin reason, break_glass flag and a separate approval scope) as the in-repo break-glass pattern
sandbox-manager WithSpaceReadVerifier gating of process reads as the model for an admin-read verifier
constraints: Room conversation content is owned by Model Plane session-core (threads carry space_id and per-row audience revisions) and is readable only with a Control-signed per-member thread:read decision; Application Plane holds membership, presence, read-marker and binding projections, not the transcript. Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL, so compliance read must be its own Control decision class verified by the owner plane, not a role check or Application export. ZDR runs are not persisted (session-core retention class), so ZDR rooms have nothing to export and the product must say so. session-core run-action scope is explicitly not a transcript API, and any break-glass must stay separate from agent authority and never impersonate an agent. Export is a mass-exfiltration path and needs dual approval plus audit-core evidence and affected-user notice. Legal holds today cover personal-Space deletion only.
approachAdjustment: Move room-content export from "Application Plane projections" to Model Plane session-core behind a new Control-signed compliance-export decision (reason, scope, expiry, approver) verified the way verify_thread_read_space_decision is; Application contributes membership metadata only, and Data Plane room search needs an owner-plane feed rather than a direct read. Build in this order: generalise the existing Control hold (after a message retention sweeper exists), then the compliance decision class and export, then sandbox-manager admin RPCs (hibernate, snapshot, kill, read-with-reason) that need new service-principal or admin-decision auth because current RPCs are org and owner scoped. Information barriers remain deferred.
effortNote: Unchanged. Recommend splitting into three L-sized rows: hold generalisation plus retention enforcement, compliance export decision plus session-core export, and sandbox break-glass admin RPCs.
verdictReason: Status partial is right and the Control hold is a real asset, but the item places room export in the Application Plane when session-core owns the transcript, and it understates that holds have no retention sweeper to act on; reword placement, ordering and split.

exactGap: No call, SFU, WebRTC or meeting-record code exists in the audited apps (search for livekit, mediasoup, RTCPeerConnection, jitsi and huddle hit only documents), so there is nothing to record. The only MediaRecorder is the dictation recorder in voice-recorder.ts, the only raw-AV storage is a docs-only Channel Plane plan (MinIO, uploaded files first), and the MinIO CAS bucket is a page-image bucket that Data Plane can only delete from. The Space product definition lists huddles as a non-goal.
reuse: Channel Plane meeting-intelligence ownership table (capture to Quarry evidence, MinIO raw AV, ASR in Model Plane, storage through Data Plane contracts)
spaceDeletionReceipts.ts per-owner receipt states as the pattern for an expiry or purge receipt
Control space_legal_holds as the retention fence for recordings
interactive_retention_consumer.go as the shape of an expiry job
constraints: The item depends on F-t1-029 first-party calls, which do not exist, and the Space definition (updated 2026-08-16) says Verevon will not run a chat-feature parity race on huddles. Recordings are persistent raw media and must be refused for ZDR orgs and honour Control policy. The documented meeting path is external-meeting capture by a Channel Plane connector into Quarry evidence submission, with Channel Plane docs-only and not to be assumed. The existing CAS bucket and its erasure code are document-scoped page images, so a recording store needs its own bucket or prefix, key layout, lifecycle rules and erasure path.
approachAdjustment: The proposed "SFU egress under an Application Plane call record" presumes a first-party call stack that is not planned. If recording is wanted before calls, the only aligned near-term shape is uploaded recordings registered as Data Plane documents (the meeting-intelligence MVP); first-party egress should wait for a call-stack ADR that names the SFU owner (Infra) and the call record owner (Application).
effortNote: L only after calls exist and only for the storage, state machine, indicator and expiry job; an SFU egress pipeline would push it to XL.
verdictReason: Absent status is right, but it is entirely conditional on a call feature that does not exist and that the product definition lists as a non-goal; it should be demoted behind transcripts and any call ADR rather than carried as a W5 build item.

exactGap: The server half already ships: Model Plane model-gateway emits a turn_timing SSE event (phases, first-token and other marks, ids and durations only) before the terminal frame, and chat-client.ts parses it and hands it to an onTurnTiming handler; browser-clock phase marks exist only as a test helper (tests/e2e/product-phase-timing.ts). Missing: no traceparent or client enter, ack, first-frame or resync events in the SPA (requestJson in http.ts and streamChat add none), the Frontend gateway has only a method-and-uri TraceLayer span and a Prometheus latency histogram with no W3C propagation to Control or Model, and playwright.config.ts has no performance project or Event Timing assertions. traceparent is already honoured in Data Plane retrieval-engine-rs and Quarry otel, so a propagation convention exists elsewhere in the repo.
reuse: model-gateway turn_timing clock and SSE event (server phases and first-token mark) and chat-client parseTurnTiming/onTurnTiming for the server side
tests/e2e/product-phase-timing.ts browser performance.now stamping of stream reads as the base for client marks and a perf spec
gateway observability.rs track_metrics middleware to extend with a request-id or trace label
Data Plane retrieval-engine-rs gRPC interceptor and Quarry quarryotel as copyable traceparent handling
http.ts requestJson and gateway upstream.rs proxy_json and send_with_retry as the two injection points, plus streamChat for the Space send path
constraints: Telemetry must carry ids and timings only (ZDR); turn_timing already follows this and its doc forbids mixing gateway and browser clocks, so a Grok-style enter_epoch_ms wall-clock subtraction conflicts with the existing design and should be replaced by client performance.now marks joined to the server record by request id or traceparent. Control (Go) and Model (Rust) services do not read traceparent today, so propagation into them is separate per-plane work with no cross-plane DB. The Space composer reaches the gateway through the chat stream and AG-UI routes, so the header must be forwarded there as well as through proxy_json. Playwright is configured with one worker and real dev stacks, so budgets need a stable CI environment.
approachAdjustment: Reword as the client half: add traceparent plus performance.now marks (enter, ack, first frame, missing row, resync) in http.ts and streamChat, forward the header in the gateway, correlate with the existing turn_timing by request id, and add a Playwright perf project using the Event Timing API. Treat full trace propagation into user-core and model-gateway as a separate follow-up that copies the retrieval-engine-rs interceptor. Do not describe server timing as missing.
effortNote: M holds for the client half plus gateway forwarding and a perf project; propagation interceptors in Control and Model Plane would add roughly one M per plane (L in total).
verdictReason: Partial is right, but the gap text must credit the shipped server turn_timing and the existing test-side browser phase timing, and the wall-clock enter_epoch_ms approach conflicts with the repo own same-clock rule.

exactGap: Browser echo cancellation, noise suppression and auto gain are enabled only for the dictation recorder (VOICE_AUDIO_CONSTRAINTS); voice mode is tap-to-talk dictation plus read-aloud with only an Enter-to-send keydown handler on its transcript textarea, so there is no push-to-talk. There is no call media to measure, and the Frontend src has no wakeLock, beforeunload, Notification, service worker or protocol-handler code and no PWA manifest. Run feedback already exists as a good, acceptable or poor rating with a free-text note (agentRuns.rate, orchestrator-core feedback_ratings), so only reason codes are missing.
reuse: VOICE_AUDIO_CONSTRAINTS and the voice-recorder/VoiceModeDialog pair for in-tab push-to-talk
Convex agentRuns.rate mutation, agentRuns rating fields and orchestrator-core feedback_ratings for a reason-code feedback record on agent runs
SpaceApprovalPanel and space-live-work own-stream state as the source for a busy-reason registry
constraints: Every call-specific part (getStats health panel, call sounds, Join notification, A/V enhancement on call tracks) depends on F-t1-029 first-party calls, which do not exist, and the Space definition lists huddles and notification polish as a non-goal. Call and voice telemetry must stay aggregate and no voice profile or biometric-like data may be stored. Feedback reason codes must be normalised in model-gateway like the existing rating vocabulary, because feedback_ratings has a CHECK on rating values. Wake Lock support is partial and must always be released.
approachAdjustment: Split the bundle. Keep the call-independent slices that help the agent-first room now: a busy-reason registry with a beforeunload guard (shared with the web-first part of F-t1-090), reason codes added to the existing run rating, a hold-to-talk key in VoiceModeDialog, and Wake Lock while a long run or approval is being watched. Defer getStats call health, call sounds, Join notification actions and A/V processing until a call stack exists, and demote them.
effortNote: M for the call-independent slices combined (each S to M); the call-only slices are not estimable until calls exist.
verdictReason: Most of the bundle presupposes non-existent calls and cuts against a stated non-goal; only the call-independent slices (busy guard, run feedback reason codes, hold-to-talk, wake lock) are worth carrying and they should be extracted.

exactGap: No native shell exists: index.html is a plain web entry, the parity audit confirms no Electron or Tauri app and no PWA manifest, Endpoint Plane is a native Rust remote-desktop host agent rather than a chat shell, and apps/remote-dev is a dev harness. The web-first close guard is also absent, since verevonv3 has no beforeunload or pagehide handler and SpaceRoomComposer neither persists drafts nor warns on unsent text or a running own stream. The scan candidate start_ai_run in browser.rs is the browser-agent run route, not the Space composer endpoint, which is the chat stream and AG-UI routes with Space context injection.
reuse: SpaceRoomComposer streamChat path through gateway chat/streams.rs and ag_ui.rs, which already inject Control-issued Space decisions from a space_ref alone
space-live-work ownStream and Space approval state to decide when a close guard is warranted
voice-recorder and VoiceModeDialog for push-to-talk once a key-up event is available
constraints: The browser may choose only space_ref and the gateway strips every forged authority field (FORGED_SPACE_AUTHORITY_FIELDS), so a quick composer must go through the same Space-injection path and land in the personal Space, never a separate run API with client-authored authority. ZDR and org context are applied server-side on that shared path (apply_org_zdr_posture after the Space injectors) from the validated session, so the shell webview must reuse the session and must not hold its own credentials. The shell depends on F-t1-073 and nothing in the repo provides it today. Global push-to-talk and always-on-top windows are shell-only; the close guard is a Frontend Plane web change.
approachAdjustment: Split into (1) a web-first guard, S: beforeunload when the Space composer holds unsent text or an own stream is running, optionally with draft persistence, shippable now; and (2) the shell-only quick composer, global shortcut and window state, which wait for F-t1-073 and should target the chat stream and AG-UI routes, not browser.rs start_ai_run. Define push-to-talk once with F-t1-086 rather than twice.
effortNote: M for the shell-only conveniences assuming the shell exists (the shell itself is XL elsewhere); the web-first guard is S and a quick win.
verdictReason: Absent is right for the shell part, but the item misses that the web-first guard is also unbuilt, and its implied endpoint (the scan pointed at the browser-agent run route) is wrong; split the cheap web slice from the shell-gated slice.
